questions.question: Give two examples of energy being transferred from a source to where it is needed.
questions.expected_answer: Any two, for example: light and heat from the Sun reaching Earth; electricity travelling along wires from a power station to a home; movement of the wind turning a windpump; energy from a battery to a torch bulb; energy from food to our muscles.

questions.question: Name the input energy and the useful output energy of a kettle, a radio and a torch.
questions.expected_answer: Kettle: input electricity, output heat. Radio: input electricity, output sound. Torch: input stored energy from the battery, giving electricity; output light.

questions.question: What is wasted energy? Give an example.
questions.expected_answer: Wasted energy is output energy that we do not want and cannot use, usually heat or sound that spreads into the surroundings. For example, an old light bulb gets hot, so much of its energy is wasted as heat; a tractor's engine gives out heat and noise.
